feedback: This candidate changes only controller.ki, from 0.3 to 0.9, relative to the best raced design (iteration 1, score 71.2). Iteration 1 showed every trial still going off track with max_error about 0.063 m, just past the 0.06 m limit, one line-loss event per run, and steering_oscillation about 0.15 (iteration 1 data). That pattern is a steady bias rather than jitter, which fits the fixed 2% motor mismatch the integral term is meant to cancel. Iteration 0 (ki 0) had the same drift, and iteration 1 raised progress on all three tracks after ki went from 0 to 0.3, so the integral direction is supported. kp 3.0, kd 0.15 and base_speed 1.3 are unchanged, so the race isolates the ki change. Geometry is unchanged, and body_width cannot widen the limit (the 0.06 m floor binds). The integral is clamped at ±2, so ki 0.9 has bounded effect. Risks to check in the telemetry: a larger integral may overshoot on bends, which would show as rising steering_oscillation, and base_speed 1.3 is still below the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s, so completion is not expected. This is early exploration with nine iterations after this one, so racing is more informative than another read. After the race, decide from the measurements. If max_error falls and line_loss_events reach 0 with progress near 0.995, raise base_speed toward 1.8. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.2, raise kd toward 0.25 before changing ki or kp. If max_error still sits near 0.06 with a steady bias and no oscillation, raise ki further (up to about 1.5) before touching kp.
requested_changes: Keep controller.kp at 3.0, kd at 0.15 and base_speed at 1.3 for this race, so the ki change is isolated; iteration 1 (ki 0.3) drifted to max_error about 0.063 m, and this test checks whether ki 0.9 brings that below 0.06 m.

If the race shows progress at or near 0.995 with no line loss, raise controller.base_speed from 1.3 toward 1.8, since iteration 1 showed the off-track drift was the binding failure and speed becomes the limit only once the robot stays on the line.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 (iteration 1 was about 0.15), raise controller.kd from 0.15 toward 0.25 before changing ki or kp, because a larger integral can cause bend overshoot.
